I know that [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] is awaiting some legal advice from PT exertnal counsel (SPASS) on the wider issue of scooters fines in PT, in particular for the ones which have accumulated so far.

However, I would like to set expectations and responsibilities here. These fines are a global issues for the Rentals vertical unfortunately - however this should be *primarily addressed by Ops and CS* and *a process should be created to handle these fines quickly when they come in*. You might also seek some guidance from Product Counsel ([~accountid:61cc1c959ee70a00680edd89] and [~accountid:626fb920f42962006fde4c04] ) to leverage what’s being done in other countries, however I do not think that the Global Field Legal Team can help you proceed each and single fine.

By way of comparison, I understand that *Rentals in Germany* have recruited one person, whose responsibility and role is to handle the fines - perhaps [~accountid:5bf7a8fb7ffaec527a023256] can confirm this?

I have also checked with DE Legal Counsel and she explained that the *proposed process in DE is as follows*:

{quote}1. Local Ops will check all fines as they arrive and appeal those that are obviously improperly issued (not parked properly, VOI scooter etc).
2. Fines that users are responsible for will be entered into the Ops Admin Panel and in most cases paid by Bolt.
3. If a fine meets pre-defined criteria, it will either be passed onto users or Bolt will bear the cost (e.g. fines would NOT be passed on if GPS/accelerometer data suggests the scooter was moved or if user photos look good or if first offense or whatever - for product/business to decide)
4. Where fine is passed onto a user, they will be presented with an in-app pop up together with an email notifying them of the fine and requesting payment. They can either authorise payment or be locked out of the Rentals function within the app until the fine is paid. Alternatively, there should be some appeals process internally at first where CS compares photos or other mitigating factors.
5. If no action by the user is taken after a reasonable amount of time, the account might be blocked, partially blocked (e.g. just Rentals), negative Bolt balance applied, invoice raised or potentially referred to debt collectors.{quote}

I hope this helps and, if I may, I would suggest the PT team approaches the DE team to align on approach and next steps.

I also understand that in other countries, the *PP/Reg Team* (aka [~accountid:60ec731b2f97d50069db1627] in PT) is *discussing this issue with the local authorities* to ensure that the processes that are put in place internally match the local authorities' expectations.

Of course, [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] will revert once she obtains some elements of responses from PT external counsel, but I do not think that Legal can assist with these specific fines / ticket.

Hi [~accountid:60c7025b5c64b10071aef787] , I gave it some thought, and I want to decline this request, mainly because there are too many results and we'll potentially release bystander information I just feel releasing this info is not proportional nor justified considering the circumstances of the request. Let’s reuse an answer we provided in another case. 

----

Rest assured it's always the intention of Bolt to disclose personal data to the police wherever it is permitted to do so. Bolt takes its law enforcement cooperation responsibilities seriously and the company regularly makes disclosures to law enforcement agencies in response to such requests.

We trust you understand that any disclosure of personal data from Bolt for law enforcement purposes must still comply with the UK GDPR, and in particular, a lawful basis is required at Art.6. The disclosure must be necessary and proportionate to the stated purpose. While Data Protection Act 2018 provides some exemptions from the application of UK GDPR, the disclosure needs to be connected to the investigated issue.

The nature of the request is speculative enquiry and hence widely exploratory. The link between requested data points and given data points (addresses) with criminal activity to Bolt operations is vague and based on assumptions about what specific data points could indicate.  Especially as the requested data is wide in scope and the information given to us covers busy commuting areas where the loss of third parties' right to privacy is inevitably affected. The potential, even inadvertent, loss of the third party's right to privacy must be warranted in these circumstances. 

Compliance with the current disclosure request conflicts with other legal obligations with which Bolt is required to comply i.e. data protection. Should you wish to narrow the scope of the requested data further to relate to the specific incident being investigated (shooting incident) or demonstrate (at a high level) why the loss of privacy in this instance is warranted and required to assist in that investigation, then please do let us know.

Hey Daniel, thanks for confirming. Out of 17 transactions that have been stopped, we received today 7 confirmations that payout has been released.

_To ensure we can prevent this from happening in the future, is this sort of “check“ required regularly? We’d like to avoid this situation at any cost. Thank you!_

Such checks are conducted to 100% transactions inside European Union by all financial institutions to comply with sanctions legislation. If Citibank now whitelists this recipient + account they would be able to process transactions to this recipient with no / or minor delays. Still time to time there can be more thorough checks (especially considering that the entity name is HOMS and they want to double check whether beneficiaries are connected to Syria or not). 

In recent months in general we see heavy drop of number of sanctions cases / payouts that are being stopped and if it happens the responses/resolutions are quick. Citibank had massive delays during summer due to war in Ukraine and continuous new sanctions rules it caused etc. Basically this case fell between the cracks of their processes and thus we faced such a long period of resolution.

The reason this feature was designed for the active order screen (right after the driver has accepted), is allegedly due to the lack of space on the acceptance screen. To note, UK drivers can cancel the order without any consequences so although it would be more convenient to have it on the acceptance screen, the impact stays the same.

Hi [~accountid:624407b42e101c006a8d8cf6] 

Following our conversation, I’ve revised the contract draft and below are some tips and general guidance from the employment lawyer to mitigate the reclassification risk and hence the contractual relationship with the 3PL being considered as an employment agreement. 

* +*General overview : service provider vs employee*+  

According to French employment law, to be considered as an independent contractor, the service provider shall have:

* the possibility to build up its own clientele;

* to freely set up his fares, and

* to freely determine the conditions of exercise of the service provided.



French Courts ruled that a contractual relationship is considered as an employment relationship, if the following elements are demonstrated:

* the provision of work,

* the payment of a remuneration, and

* the existence of a link of subordination characterized as "the performance of work under the authority of an employer who has the power to give orders and instructions, to control their execution and to sanction the failures of his subordinate".

French Courts determine the existence of a subordination link between the platforms and their contractors based on a bundle of indices, such as: providing of instructions, monitoring of worker, imposing working hours etc.

* +*Tips*+ 

# Bolt shall not expressly indicates that the Contractor shall collaborate for the performance of services and +comply with its instructions.+
# The service provider must use +his/her own tools+ to perform the services. → to mitigate the risk, Bolt software and IT tools shall be granted for security purposes only. 
# The service provider must organize his/her work as he/she wants and Bolt shall not impose him/her +working hours and full availability.+
#  The service provider shall organize and monitor his +warehouses+ freely.
# The service provider's +fees+ shall be determined on a flat-rate basis for the performance of any specific mission and not on a monthly basis (such as employees) → please avoid mentioning that the +invoice+ will be provided on a monthly basis.
# Foreseeing +liquidated damages+ in the event of poor performance of the services could be seen as a form of direction and sanction powers on the service provider which are typical of a employer-employee relationship → to limit the reclassification risk, we recommend Bolt not to apply liquidated damages if the service provider fails to reach the 20% target.
# The +Service Levels+ measurement system implemented to assess the provider’s performance on specific targets and  the +bonus/malus system+  may significantly increase the reclassification risk. In case of dispute,  the judges could consider that Bolt exercises its power of control, direction and sanction towards the service provider’s personnel, whose performance is evaluated as it was Bolt’s own personnel. In addition, from an employment law perspective, the malus mechanism could be considered as a financial sanction which is prohibited.

In addition, as a general rule applicable across all West EU, we strongly recommend you ask Carbio to designate one +“Service Coordinator”+ to act as the primary contact person for such entity with respect to the performance of the services. All communications and instructions relating to the services should be directed to Service Coordinator who will then dispatch them to the rest of Carbio’s personnel.

We strongly recommend following these tips carefully.

Should you have any questions/doubts, please do let us know.

Thank you

Slack message with Jose: I asked for an outline of our current thought processes with refunds and when we issue these. 

*Main reasons for refunds:*

* Overcharge - Usually Partial refund

* Driver took longer route -

* If estimate was 20€ and the final charge was 30€ we would refund 10€ - instead of full refund for a job completed.

* Driver did not start or end the trip correctly
* Tolls of additional fees (cleaning fee- could of not been added to the estimate
* Surge - High demand 1x, 2x normal price etc

* Usually if 1st report we would educate and provide a small compensation

* If any of the above is 50% or more than the estimate we would full refund

* Bad experience - Usually Partial refund

* ETA - Long pick up time
* Rude Driver
* Safety cases Full refund - depends on the severity of the case

 _We are therefore also assuming that Bolt does_ +_not_+ _provide transportation services, charging the drivers – who are presumably self-employed, therefore not Bolt employees presumably, and VAT registered – a fee (possibly deducted from the amount collected per invoice by each said driver) for the lead generation services Bolt provides to the drivers._

 _We note that we are engaged by Bolt Malta – is this the company that provides these lead generation services or is a non-Maltese resident company forming part of the group doing so?  Please clarify the role of Bolt Malta and that of any other group entity, if so, involved in the provision of the service to the drivers._

_Meanwhile, we are also assuming that Bolt Malta has applied for, and obtained from the VAT Department locally, what is referred to as an “EXO number” i.e. basically permission, by the VAT Department, following an audit of its system, to use this system to issue VAT invoices, as opposed to physical fiscal receipts (via the booklet that presumably each driver has should the system not function e.g. because of a technical hitch), to the driver’s taxable person and its non-taxable person clients alike._

FR Business would like to hide some price components in the RH fare cards (the screen with price breakdown  appearing once you select the ride and click on the total price).

* *per min amount/min*
* Wait time fee/min
* Cancellation flat fee
* Seats ( number)

I’ve been told that pricing per min and per km is “static” info within Paris area meaning that there’s no algorithm triggered and recalculating fares per km and min depending on the time of the day, demand and other factors.

Rider would be given with the total estimated price before riding ( excluding any journey variation and additional paid waiting time)  but less detailed. Technically, the rider would be able to calculate actual price per min and per km from the receipt, but I guess the requirement is to provide transparent and granular information upfront.

Hi [~accountid:5d91ad8a1d47a50c34d48412] 

Just following up here to let you know we have prepared a guidance note on the use of courier campaigns / bonuses: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rXJFA8_V5EbCK6pIi3HxuzXmF0r5yR1r-Xk017zIHGs/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rXJFA8_V5EbCK6pIi3HxuzXmF0r5yR1r-Xk017zIHGs/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] (NB this makes reference to Poland specifically, but it is applicable to all countries)


Your proposal (“get X if you deliver Y orders within Z time period”) is OK from a legal perspective, subject to a couple of conditions:

a) We should avoid using the phrase “guaranteed earnings”, and 

b) The target number of orders within the required time period must be achievable (based on real data). If we are setting targets that are completely unachievable, the campaign looks more like a mechanism to exercise control over couriers rather than a true incentive.

We would also advise that when setting the “bonus” amount, we take into account a calculation of the actual average earning per 100 orders, so that the difference between the reality and 400 euros (in the example you gave) would be as little as possible (because in the end, this is direct payment by Bolt to the courier from its own funds, which presents a higher reclassification risk).

Of course, let me elaborate on the above!

POS Integration:

Each restaurant is working with a POS software provider. In Cyprus there could be more than 10 POS providers each having their own restaurants they are working with. Some large chains could actually develop their own POS system like ICs. 

We are able to integrate with those providers and automatically send the orders received from Bolt Food in their POS without them having to punch in the orders received from the tablet which saves them a significant amount of time. 

Up to now Bolt wanted a 2-way integration (meaning that the orders are sent out in their POS system but information from the POS can also been sent on the app). Wolt and Foody have been integrating with providers on a 1-way integration (meaning that orders are only sent to their POS but their POS is not sending any information on the app)

Our former colleague Michael Georgiou discussed with Gladius and since their share of the market was quite large, Bolt decided to invest the time and integrate with Gladius on a 1-way integration.

The reason we discussed with Gladius was because their client base was either 

a) already on the Bolt Food app and generated a significant share of our GMV

b) restaurants which we were trying to onboard and integration was a big blocker for us



Requests:

We are not in communication with POS providers per-se but rather the restaurants themselves reach out to us and ask for integration. What is advised from HQ is as follows: 

We focus on providers, not POSs, meaning we prioritise integrations based on GMV of providers requesting integration rather than GMV coverage of the POS. We go with a top-down approach. 

# International chains (IC): doing all requested integrations
# Key accounts (KA) and local heroes (LH): +all integrations which add or retain 5% of a country’s GMV.+
# SMBs: currently, out of scope. 

*Why?* Biggest pain POS integrations is solving is manually copying orders to POS, which is why we concentrate on the ones with larger volumes => biggest pain.  

*Adding or retaining 5% country’s GMV* means integration unblocks signing a provider(s) bringing 5% GMV or is requested by provider(s) already generating 5% GMV.

You can find more details here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BF/pages/2941981173/Integrations|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BF/pages/2941981173/Integrations|smart-link] 



VDL:

We have no issues whatsoever in assessing VDL integration. This could actually be beneficial to us, provided that the above can be covered.

Fleet docs query migrated to Presto. There are no placeholders in there as [~accountid:5d7b6987656e2a0dbab30492] had. Just sample values to make sure it runs.

{code:sql}-- doc
with doc as (
    select id as doc_id,
        created_date as created,
        document_type_id,
        status,
        external_item_type,
        file_name,
        external_id,
        cast(external_id / 1000000 as varchar) as one,
        cast(((external_id / 1000000) * 1000000 - external_id) / -1000 as varchar) as two,
        cast(external_id - (external_id / 1000000 * 1000000) - ((((external_id / 1000000) * 1000000 - external_id) / -1000) * 1000) as varchar) as three
    from ng_public.fleet_documents_document
    where created_date between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-04-01')
-- doc_type
,doc_type as (
    select document_collection_id,
        type,
        id
    from ng_public.fleet_documents_document_type
    )
-- collection
,collection as (
    select id from ng_public.fleet_documents_document_collection
    )
-- Get collection names where the doc type of interest is present in
,top_collection as (
    select collection.id as collection_id,
        row_number() over (order by count(doc_id) desc) as top_collection
    from collection
        join doc_type on doc_type.document_collection_id=collection.id
        join doc on doc.document_type_id=doc_type.id
    where doc_type.type = 'gh_roadworthiness_sticker_car'
    group by 1)
-- Get correct labels
,correct_docs as
    (select
        'fleet_document' as source_type,
        doc_id,
        'fleet_documents/' || doc.external_item_type || '/' || doc.one || '/' || doc.two || '/' || doc.three || '/' || doc.file_name as s3_key,
        doc_type.type as doc_key,
        row_number() over (partition by doc_type.type order by random()) as row_number
    from doc
        join doc_type on doc.document_type_id = doc_type.id
        join collection on doc_type.document_collection_id=collection.id
    where doc_type.type = 'gh_roadworthiness_sticker_car'
        and collection.id = (select collection_id from top_collection where top_collection=1)
    )
 -- Get incorrect document types for creating labels
,incorrect_doc_types as (
    select type as doc_type,
        count(doc_id) as count
    from doc_type
        join collection on doc_type.document_collection_id=collection.id
        join doc on doc.document_type_id=doc_type.id
    where collection.id = (select collection_id from top_collection where top_collection=1)
        and doc_type.type != 'gh_roadworthiness_sticker_car'
    group by 1
    order by count desc)
-- Get incorrect documents
,incorrect_docs as (
    select
        'fleet_document' as source_type,
        doc.doc_id,
        'fleet_documents/' || doc.external_item_type || '/' || doc.one || '/' || doc.two || '/' || doc.three || '/' || doc.file_name as s3_key,
        doc_type.type as doc_key,
        row_number() over (partition by doc_type.type order by random()) as row_number
    from doc
        join doc_type on doc.document_type_id = doc_type.id
    where doc_type.type in (select distinct doc_type from incorrect_doc_types)
    )
(select source_type, 
     s3_key, 
     doc_key
from correct_docs
where row_number <= 10)
union all
(select source_type, 
     s3_key, 
     doc_key
from incorrect_docs
where row_number <= 2
limit 10){code}

Hey [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35], thank you for looping us in!

The global approach is indeed to ensure more transparency for the riders, and the initiative to reduce transparency for consumers is not welcome from legal perspective. This is partially due to the fact that the fares shown upfront may still sometimes appear different in the end, for example, if: 

* rider is applied wait time fee in the beginning of the ride (rider has shown up late),
* rider requests a stop in the middle of the journey (this feature is currently being rolled out in some markets).

If the upfront fee is different from what we have shown the rider in the app upfront, the breakdown in the email after the ride will not save us from the arguments on the lack of transparency towards consumers. Therefore, I would suggest we don’t unnecessarily reduce transparency if we are not able to show the final prices upfront.

In addition, there might be some legal obstacles to this arising from local legislation. For example, in Estonia such breakdown is mandatory to show to the rider upfront. But I will leave this one to you, just wanted to flag it here for clarity 🙂

Hey team,

So there is no actual issue here. This is a rounding glitch that is not unique to Bolt. To explain it briefly, we show the balance entries with 2 decimals in admin (i.e. 31.78), however in the system it has more decimals (i.e. 31,784). And in Driver Portal, it is shown with 1 decimal only (i.e. 31.8). So when decimals get less, the system rounds it up/down to the closest number. 

So you can let the driver know that the exact calculation adds up to 474.28. The reason why they see 474.3 in the Driver Portal (and also why we see 474.30 in Admin) is because of this rounding glitch. But, modern accounting tools are smart enough to consider this with next payouts. So, when he has actual difference, it will be compensated in following payouts anyway.

Thanks for reaching out.

I see that the error messages are 330: PAYMENT_ERROR_TEMPORARY, which means that the payment method issuer/bank is rejecting the cards, and as the bank/issuer of the card, each time, the number of errors is counted. When the number of errors reaches a certain threshold, it triggers our rules and starts to get fraud-related errors.

So, one solution for the user can be contacting their bank/issuer to solve the problem so that they don’t get the errors and consequently don’t get caught by our fraud rules. Another solution can be to continue using the existing/another payment method.

I’ll mark the ticket as “resolved”, but if the issue persists, you can notify me by tagging me on this ticket.

Best,

Dear Karina,
Each business trip should include travel order and travel report:

1. *Travel order* - should include following:
- company data (name, address)
- date of issuing (before the trip)
- travel order number
- employee name and surname
- employee education degree
- employee work place
- date of travel 
- place of travel
- prediction of how many days the trip will last
- the purpose of travel
- information about transportation (private car, business car, bus, train...)
- for car, a registration number should be noticed
- for car, starting kilometres and ending kilometre balance should be noticed
- name and signature of the person who is authorised to approve the trip

2. *Travel report* - should include following:
- company data (name, address)
- date of issuing (after the trip)
- travel report number
- employee name and surname
- an employee should provide a traveling summary explaining in short:

* what was the main purpose of his trip,
* where it was held,
* in which period it last,
* employee should present originals of invoices as proof of expenses he had during the trip (invoice for traveling expenses, accommodation expenses, taxi from/to airport),
* employee should give information whether meals were covered instead of employee,
* other relevant data (if any).



* relations of the trip (from city to city)
* time of arrival and departure
* time of crossing border for trips abroad
* number of hours spent
* number and amount of daily allowance (split by country if the trip include more than 1 country) 
* data about car usage and kilometres actually spent
* list of expenses for refund (invoices of expenses should be attached)
* total amount of expenses related to business trip
* amount of advance payment
* amount which has to be paid to employee
* signature of employee confirming that the data is correct
* signature of liquidator confirming that the expenses are approved for payout

We hope this helps, please let us know in case there is any other explanation necessary.

Kind regards,

Marina

The missing roads job was failing with {{failed to allocate memory}} on driver when multiple cities were run:

{noformat}OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM warning: INFO: os::commit_memory(0x00007f9de6180000, 12470714368, 0) failed; error='Cannot allocate memory' (errno=12)
Command exiting with ret '1' {noformat}

It can be seen form the image bellow how the memory was increasing up to total host memory, each step increase align with processing of a new city (looks like a memory leak, but it is not, see bellow the explanation). 

!Screenshot 2022-11-09 at 10.10.06.png|width=752,height=445!

The missing roads driver was configured with xmx=500g  (using --driver-memory=500g), and the entire host has 128g of RAM. 

Reducing the driver memory to 64g fixed the issue:

!Screenshot 2022-11-10 at 10.10.25.png|width=745,height=440!

It looks that when JVM was configured with 500g it tried to increase the memory instead of trying to clean it up (most likely to optimise application runtime, as the GC time is more expensive).

----

*How the spark driver memory may be configured?*

Generally spark support settings parameters using {{conf/spark-defaults.conf}}, passing them as {{spark-submit}} command line options, or setting them programmatically through {{SparkConf}} in runtime. However, when running jobs in client mode, the “spark.driver.memory” must not be set through the {{SparkConf}} directly in your application, because the driver JVM has already started at that point. Instead, please set this through the {{--driver-memory}} command line option or in your default properties file.

Properties set directly on the SparkConf take highest precedence, then flags passed to {{spark-submit}} or {{spark-shell}}, then options in the {{spark-defaults.conf}} file.

*How the spark driver memory is configured for missing roads (and for other jobs too)?*

In our code base we set the driver memory in two places:

# we set it to {{64g}} at [runtime using SparkConf|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/dac29065381601f71794352ff8407a4e747bd349/common3/src/main/java/ee/mtakso/spark/common/framework/MTaksoSparkSession.java#L211-L219], the property is defined in [job.config.base.yaml|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/115e5f35add1b67f912396b49252f5981fa66257/jobs/map-metrics/src/main/resources/job.config.base.yaml#L29-L30] file.
# we set it  to{{500g}} by setting it as [command line options of spark-submit |https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/0b0812060840c10f4a53132a7d7e6d00ee006c77/infra/template/job-step.json#L9-L10]command.

As we run the jobs in [client mode|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/0b0812060840c10f4a53132a7d7e6d00ee006c77/infra/template/job-step.json#L7-L8], according to the above spark configuration options, the option one we use is useless and the second one is used. (Unfortunately, when spark application is checked it will show the wrong value spark.driver.memory=64g).

----

Ideally we should set the properties in a single way to avoid any confusions regarding what property is really used when spark is launched. For example, we also configure the {{executor-memory}} in two different places, via spark-submit as command line parameter {{--executor-memory 8g}} and at [runtime|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/115e5f35add1b67f912396b49252f5981fa66257/jobs/map-metrics/src/main/resources/job.config.base.yaml#L27] {{spark.executor.memory=35g}} (second option takes precedence but it is a bit confusing for people not knowing the configuration precedence, or simply not finding both places in code).

select * from (select *, 
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id, id ORDER BY distance_from_dropoff) nearest_rack
from(
select 
o.vehicle_id,
o.id,
o.created,
o.last_update,
o.vehicle_lat,
o.vehicle_lng,
o.dropoff_lat,
o.dropoff_lng,
o.finish_reason,
r.id as dropoff_rack_id,
ST_Distance(to_spherical_geography(ST_Point(o.dropoff_lng, o.dropoff_lat)),to_spherical_geography(ST_Point(r.lng, r.lat))) distance_from_dropoff
from ng_rental.rental_order_order o
left join ng_rental.rental_order_charging_rack_state r on o.city_id=r.city_id AND ST_Distance(to_spherical_geography(ST_Point(o.dropoff_lng, o.dropoff_lat)),to_spherical_geography(ST_Point(r.lng, r.lat)))<200
where o.city_id in (1,1230,1040,3,9,13,2,278,1395,209)
and o.created>date'2022-10-01'
and o.state='finished'
and o.finish_reason = 'connection_to_charging_rack'
order by o.vehicle_id asc, o.created asc)
) where nearest_rack=1
),

Key points about adding a source code extension to Xcode.

* There is not much documentation about it. Apple official [link|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcodekit/creating_a_source_editor_extension]. Also, there is a good guide [here|https://nshipster.com/xcode-source-extensions/]
* Extension is sandboxed. As a result, you cannot access the path of the selected file or working directory, only the file's content. Most of the extensions resolve this issue with the companion app where the user sets the working directory. As an example take a look at [MockGenerator|https://github.com/seanhenry/SwiftMockGeneratorForXcode]
* There is a trick with AppleScript to get the workspace directory, but I didn’t manage to make it work. It worked in AppleScriptEditor but didn’t work during debugging. Here is [the code|https://github.com/seanhenry/SwiftMockGeneratorForXcode/blob/master/Shared/XcodeProjectPathFinder.swift#L16].

*Conclusion:* 

* CDC nodes must be in downstream to avoid lag to DR TiDB cluster
* We must also have CDC nodes in upstream for Kafka clients
* No way in v6.1 to lock/bind a changefeed to a CDC node/specific region
* In v6.3, there is now concept of CDC clusters, allowing one cluster in upstream and one cluster in downstream, and changefeed can choose which cluster to connect to. 

* {{ticdc_cluster_id}}: Specifies the TiCDC cluster ID corresponding to the service. If this field is not specified, the service joins the default TiCDC cluster. This field only takes effect in TiDB *v6.3.0* or later versions.

Hey Valeria, 

Thanks for sharing this! I have a lot to cover here so I’ll number the topics 😅 

1️⃣ *Pre-authorisation*
I just [shared with the CS team|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C01GPNU0V50/p1668166388906989] that for user reports of pre-authorisation not being released, we can follow [+🚗 Rider reports pre-authorisation not being released+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7109163016850]. The issue type to select here is _I’m having issues with a refund_. I’ve updated the Car-sharing user issues list accordingly as well.

I also wanted to establish the correct understanding: pre-authorisation and 3DS check are *two separate things*:

* [A pre-authorisation|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005100694] is *Bolt* *reserving* a particular amount to check if the payment method selected is valid and if there are sufficient funds;
* [3DS check|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360019018359] is a *card issuer (bank) initiated* authentication. It’s a mandatory requirement that Bolt has to meet but it’s not initiated by us.

It’s important to communicate this to agents and ensure they follow the correct procedures and not these two different things up. If we need to look into additional training for this, please request this from Edwina Mogale. 🙂 

2️⃣ *Unclear error messages*

330: PAYMENT_ERROR_TEMPORARY - this is a 3DS check-related error.
329: CHALLENGE CANCELLED - this pre-authorisation error.

In both cases, the payment method issuer rejected the payment. The solution for the user is to contact the bank/issuer or use another payment method. I’ll make sure to clarify these errors in the relevant KB articles - once it’s done, I’ll post an announcement on Slack.

3️⃣ *Deleting and re-installing the app*
The Fraud team asked to stop requesting users to delete and re-install the Bolt app in case of 3DS issues and follow the KB processes for specific 3DS check issues instead. Could you communicate this to the CS team?

Hope I covered everything - definitely let me know if you have any questions!

*Update*
On the analysis based on the feedback raised by Helder and Tyson.

*Note:* Keep in mind that, while a priori the correlation between the features and ASP can seem strong (see the example of Lisbon in the plots attached), the model used (Prophet) decomposes Time Series (temporal data) into Trend, Seasonality, Holidays and the effect of regressors; after removing the first 3 components, the relationship between the “_residual_” _(clean)_ Time Series can be completely different than between the originals.

This happens in many of the cities included in the analysis, e.g. Lisbon, where using Utilization, Online Hours (per driver) and Surge (%), which all seem correlated with ASP at first, including them in the model (either together or separately) actually worsens the forecasts’ accuracy.The main findings are:

* For all of the cities but Paris & Lagos, *when we include the features* that a priori (before decomposing the series) seem correlated with ASP, *it actually worsens the accuracy of the forecasts,* or at best, it does not affect it. This is also the case when we include only one of the features in the model at a time; in some cases, the MAPE is unaffected.
* *For Paris, including drivers’ acceptance rates in the model improves the forecasts.*
* For Lagos, including online hours in the model improves (though only marginally) the forecasts.
* However, note that for both Paris and Lagos, predicting those features based on spending is not feasible since using them does not improve the accuracy of simple models without any features. Thus, if we want to forecast ASP via these features for these cities, modeling ASP in terms of net rates is not feasible.

In addition, I have tested another approach: *modeling ASP at different net rates by forecasting GMV and Rides and then dividing one by the other.*

* The models produced in the FP cycles show that *the relationship between GMV & Rides and spending on campaigns is reasonable*.
* Early tests show *reasonable accuracies for most of the cities*, with an average MAPE of 7% without a thorough tuning.
* In addition, it has the following operational advantages:
* The curves of Rides and *ASP in terms of net rates could already be available during model selection* via plots in ML Flow.
* This information is already provided by DS each cycle. We would only have to add a hyperparameter tuning step for the models forecasting Rides and create the extra visualizations that would be displayed during model selection.

Action points & deadlines [@vladyslav.yakovenko|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U0116ENFY8G]:

* For December’s cycle
** Provide ASP forecasts (using a model without features, thus without modeling ASP in terms of net rates) for the 45 cities for which we observed that this can improve MAPEs by 2% (from 5.2% to 3.4%) w.r.t. simply using ASP (t) = ASP (t+1).
** Provide extra ASP forecasts for Paris & Lagos including drivers’ acceptance rate and online hours in their respective models.
** Do we want to extend this analysis to more cities?
** Do we want to use the 2nd approach (forecasting GMV and Rides separately) in future cycles?

The potential, even inadvertent, loss of those third parties' right to privacy must be warranted in these circumstances, which considering the exploratory nature of the request, is in our opinion not warranted._ 

_Bolt therefore cannot test for necessity and proportionality nor undertake and document an assessment for lawful disclosure - as required by law. In short, compliance with the current disclosure request conflicts with other legal obligations with which Bolt is required to comply i.e. data protection._

h2. [RFC][{color:#bf2600}Declined{color}] Separate table for invoice post-processing events/operations/actions

The post-processing invoice fields don’t fit in the new model structure – they are about the *invoice-related events*, not the invoice data itself:

{noformat}// Invoice post-processing - ideally should go to other tables
interface InvoicePostProcessingData {
  first_reminder_sent: boolean,
  is_email_sent: boolean,
  second_reminder_sent: boolean,
  send_email_ts: number,
}{noformat}

What we can do is determine the types of *events* and define the following *model* for them:

{noformat}interface InvoicePostProcessingEvent {
  id: number,
  created: number, // same as 'send_email_ts' for the 'email_sent' type
  invoice_id: number, // FK invoice_document.id
  type: 'first_reminder_sent', | 'email_sent' | 'second_reminder_sent' // easy extendable
  payload/meta?: {}, // any object with additional event metadata
  // result: 'success' | 'fail', needed if we will decide to capture failed events, but I would prefer to store here only the proof of done job i.e. success events
}{noformat}

*Pros*

* partially normalized data
* lighter {{invoive_document}} table – size and structure
* avoid redundant columns for invoice type that doesn’t have reminders, 
* easy querying for events, accessible events analytics
* easy to work in event-based communications (the replacement for the crons in the nearest future)
* no updates; selects/inserts only

*Cons*

* yet another table
* more complex querying, if we require invoices with events (hello, joins!)
* overengineering approach, if we don’t need any of its pros
* still needs migrations for adding a new value to the enum type
* harder to copy old data to the new table (need to use a hack to convert current invoice flags to events)

{code:sql}select x.country_code,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.driver_id) as count_drivers, 
sum(x.count_cash_finished_orders) as count_cash_finished_orders,
sum(x.count_not_pay) as count_not_pay,
ROUND(sum(x.count_not_pay)*1.00/NULLIF(sum(x.count_cash_finished_orders),0),2) as ratio,
sum(x.unpaid_commission) as unpaid_commission_eur
from (
with destinations_distances AS (
SELECT cod.order_id,
cod.city_id,
ROUND(great_circle_distance(co.real_destination_lat,co.real_destination_lng,cod.destination_lat,cod.destination_lng),2) AS distance_between_real_dest_and_entered_dest
FROM ng_public.company_order co 
JOIN ng_public.company_order_destination cod ON co.id = cod.order_id AND co.city_id = cod.city_id 
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
AND cod.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,co.real_destination_lat,co.real_destination_lng,cod.destination_lat,cod.destination_lng 
),
min_distance AS (
SELECT 
cod.order_id AS order_id,
cod.city_id AS city_id,
CASE WHEN d.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN MIN (d.distance_between_real_dest_and_entered_dest) END AS min_distance
FROM ng_public.company_order_destination cod
JOIN destinations_distances d ON cod.order_id = d.order_id AND cod.city_id = d.city_id
WHERE cod.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,d.order_id
),
count_orders as (
select count(DISTINCT co.id) as count_cash_finished_orders,
ot.driver_id 
from ng_public.company_order co
join ng_public.company_order_try ot on co.id = ot.order_id and co.city_id = ot.city_id and ot.state = 'finished'
left join min_distance md on co.id = md.order_id and co.city_id = md.city_id
where co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
and ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
and co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -60, current_date) as date)
and co.payment_method_type = 'default'
and md.min_distance < 1 
group by 2 
)
select pr.driver_id,
co.country_code, 
coun.count_cash_finished_orders, 
count(DISTINCT pr.order_id) as count_not_pay,
ROUND(count(DISTINCT pr.order_id)*1.00/NULLIF(coun.count_cash_finished_orders,0),2) as ratio, 
ROUND(SUM(case when a.price_review_component < 0 then COALESCE(a.price_review_component*-0.20/co.eur_currency_rate,0) else co.user_price_eur*0.20 end),2) as unpaid_commission
from ng_public.price_review_price_review pr 
join ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co on pr.order_id = co.order_id and pr.city_id = co.city_id 
left join ng_public.etl_order_pricing_components a on a.order_id = pr.order_id and a.city_id = pr.city_id
left join count_orders coun on coun.driver_id = pr.driver_id 
left join min_distance md on pr.order_id = md.order_id and pr.city_id = md.city_id
where pr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
and co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -61, current_date) as date)
and co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -60, current_date) as date)
and pr.requested_by = 'driver'
and pr.requested_reason = 'client_did_not_pay'
and md.min_distance < 1 
--and coun.count_cash_finished_orders > 100
group by 1,2,3 
having ((ROUND(count(DISTINCT pr.order_id)*1.00/NULLIF(coun.count_cash_finished_orders,0),2) > 0.3 and ROUND(SUM(co.user_price_eur)*0.20,2)>10) or (ROUND(count(DISTINCT pr.order_id)*1.00/NULLIF(coun.count_cash_finished_orders,0),2) > 0.15 and ROUND(SUM(co.user_price_eur)*0.20,2)>20))
) as x 
group by 1 {code}

It is confusing that we have executor memory configured in 2 places, as {{spark-submit}} command line argument via {{--executor-memory}} and via code setting to spark conf the {{spark.executor.memory}}. Both values can be used the one from code has higher importance. In order to avoid confusion moved this configuration to code only place.

As we run the jobs in [client mode|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/0b0812060840c10f4a53132a7d7e6d00ee006c77/infra/template/job-step.json#L7-L8], setting driver memory via SparkConf is not possible as the jvm is already started, this is the reason I removed all {{spark.driver.memory}} entries. Updated driver memory set as command line argument for `spark-submit` to fit the lower instance size for instance-group and instance-fleet configuration.



The maximum memory size of container to running driver is determined by the sum of {{spark.driver.memoryOverhead}} and {{spark.driver.memory}}.

{{spark.driver.memoryOverheadFactor}} This value defaults to 0.10 except for Kubernetes non-JVM jobs, which defaults to 0.40

{{spark.driver.memoryOverhead}} defaults to {{driverMemory * spark.driver.memoryOverheadFactor}}, with minimum of 384 MB

Info taken from: [https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html|https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html|smart-link]

Hey [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897], and thanks [~accountid:5bb1cc64c9dad04734ea835a] for looping us in!

I have not heard anything about this category in other jurisdiction ([~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7], have you?). Since we are using the same drivers for riders with corporate accounts, then I would stick to our usual logic applicable in the cases of reclassification.

* Limiting access to some category due to driver’s performance increases reclassification risk, since it gives us more control over the drivers based on their performance. This is a sign of employment relationship.
* Limiting access to some categories affects driver’s earnings. Thus, we are limiting driver’s earnings based on their performance. This goes against our narrative against reclassification that drivers' performance does not affect their earnings.
* While other filters seem to be objective, then driver score seems to be very subjective (e.g. the driver could have done nothing wrong but the rider did not rate him / her with 5 starts). We as a platform provider have no opportunity to verify whether the bad rating was provided due to the justified reasons or whether it was posted by mistake / due to subjective reasons (especially, due to racial discrimination etc).

To conclude, I don’t think it is a good idea from reclass perspective 😞 Limiting drivers' opportunities due to the behaviour that endangers passengers' safety is totally fine but limiting drivers' opportunities on the platform due to bad rider reviews would hurt our narrative against reclassification.

Hi [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] 

In Croatia there are two types of invoices:

* the ones that need to be issued in case of payment in cash (term cash includes also  card payments, except transaction to the bank account) - these invoices are fiscalized and they do not need to include any personal data of the person to whom the invoice is issued. 
* Mandatory  elements of the invoice in are following (please note that some parts apply only of the service provider is in the VAT system, but not the part related to the Personal Data):
** invoice number and date of issue,
** first and last name (title), OIB of the entrepreneur who delivered the goods or performed the services, i.e. the address of residence or habitual residence of the owner or holder of the joint activity,
** an indication of the place where the goods or services were delivered (number of the point of sale, business premises, shop, name of the shop, business unit, etc.),
** quantity and common trade name of delivered goods and type and quantity of services performed,
** the total amount of compensation and taxes classified by tax rate
Value added tax taxpayers, in addition to the listed elements of the invoice, must also specify additional elements of the invoice:
** VAT identification number of the taxpayer who delivered goods or performed services (seller),
** *first and last name (name), address, OIB or VAT identification number of the taxpayer to whom the goods were delivered or services performed (customer),*
** the date of delivery of goods or services or the date of receipt of the advance payment in the advance payment invoice, if that date can be determined and if it differs from the date of issue of the invoice,
** the unit price without VAT, i.e. the amount of compensation for delivered goods or services, classified by VAT rate,
** discounts or rebates if they are not included in the unit price,
** VAT rate,
** the amount of VAT classified by VAT rate, unless a special procedure is applied for which, in the sense of this Act, this information is excluded,
** the total amount of compensation and VAT.



Therefore, in case we issue an invoice for non cash payments we need to indicate *first and last name (name), address, OIB or VAT identification number of the taxpayer to whom the goods were delivered or services performed (customer),*

Hi Armin, yes. We launched a business category in London about 13 weeks ago.

* It is only visible to team account users.
* We haven't restricted any drivers as the aim is to increase the finish rate.
* I am aware it is available in Poland but this was more around combating the issues around safety. I believe PT are also looking at this.
* It is called the 'Business Priority Category'

*Business category overview*
What have we done to date:

* Launched 15/08/22 with the hypothesis that having a new category with increased prices would help increase finish rate (avg 56%)
* All standard category drivers have been included into the new category
* Prices initially set at 20-25% above standard
* We then increased prices on the 22/08/22 to 35% with the last price increase being on 14/10/22 to 60%

What haven't we done:

* To date we haven't announced this to either the drivers or clients. All traffic from clients has been organic. Logic was to see if we could increase the finish rate before we announce to a wider audience.

*Results*

* The number of orders have been between 100-150 in the last 8 weeks
* Outside of W/C 17/10/22 where we saw the finish rate hit 69.4% we have been achieving between 57%-64%.
* In the last three weeks we have seen the difference between the business category and standard category grow between 10%-13%. (last three weeks: business category 65.6% vs last two weeks standard (business) dropped to 50%)
* 185 unique companies have completed at least one ride since launch which accounts for 15.7% of all companies within that period

*Challenges*

* Changing the pricing hasn't had a dramatic impact on the finish rate
* ETA's - on occasion the ETA will shower higher on the business category
* Attaining data to dig deeper into the issue has been hard to come by (e.g. how many drivers have opted out of the category / avg journey distance / understanding the outcome on each session)

Hey!

Imho, this is more of a regulatory framework question. And I agree with you, it has some overlapping with Omnibus directive.

* *General limits on payment terms (per type of good)* - this is regulated by unfair practices directive and deviations from the restrictions must be agreed between the parties.		
* *Payment terms per supplier (suppliers’ turnover)* - this is regulated by unfair practices directive and deviations from the restrictions must be agreed between the parties. Also this should be checked against antitrust legislation.
* *Any specific product categories with limits on payment terms?* - this is regulated by unfair practices directive and deviations from the restrictions must be agreed between the parties.
* *Cap on selling services* - what is the scope of this question?
* *Restrictions on date of contract signing* - At least in the Baltic region, no restrictions apply.
* *Volume rebates* - Should be part of every day activities and to my best knowledge no restrictions apply.
* *Logistic bonus* - Depends on how we define it. Currently - not enough data for a meaningful answer.
* *Listing fee* - Depends on how we define it. Currently - not enough data for a meaningful answer. This could be restricted practice in antitrust sense. Should be checked against unfair practices directive.
* *Data sharing* - Depends on how we define it. Currently - not enough data for a meaningful answer. Also, data is out of our scope.
* *Time required before discount applied* - Depends on how we define it. Currently - not enough data for a meaningful answer. Supplier/BM agreement? BM/customer interaction?
* *Selling below cost price* - Depends on how we define it. Currently - not enough data for a meaningful answer. If this is BM/customer interaction, this can be done if we don't breach anti-trust legislation, is timed and we can show this as marketing cost.
* *Supplier setting selling price* - Big no-no. Unfair practices directive + this definitely breaches some anti-trust legislation and/or court practices.
* *Changes to sales price during promotion* - Supplier/BM? BM/Customer? If the latter, then it is covered in Omnibus directive. Yes, additional discount can be applied. Price going up during the campaign? Also possible, but should be checked if restrictions apply.
* *Any restrictions in relation to products with a short shelf life?*  What is the scope of this question? Discounts? Storing? Disposing?
* *Any restrictions on discounting products?* Discounting - no. Promoting - yes. 	
* *Supplier to BM requirements* - what is the scope of this question? It’s quite common to have additional requirements for agreements and this goes both ways - suppliers can have requirements for retailers. But! If it is regarding ethical and sustainable business, it’s okay. If it’s to restrict selling competitors goods - not okay. 
* *BM to customer requirements* - what is the scope of this question?	
* *HACCP requirements* - what is the scope of this question? General answer is that all countries have some sort of HACCP (or analogue) requirements on self control and leaving an audit trail. If we are talking about cold chain, the applicable restrictions are quite similar cross the market (delta t of 3’C). There are additional restrictions on frozen, thawed and cooled products, some special regulations regarding seafood etc. I don’t know if we should do a deep research on topics that are outside of BM activities (selling butchered meat? fresh oysters? unpasteurized goat milk?). 
* *Fire & hazard restrictions* - what is the scope of this question?	Can we sell kerosine, tinder and matches? Should we have special fire extinguishers (>1000V electricity, for burning fats, fire blankets, CO2 extinguishers)? Should we blow dust from the fridge’s heat exchanger? Should the rooms be equipped with automated fire alarm systems? Should we have sprinklers? 
* *Restrictions on product description / communications* -  what is the scope of this question?	 Product description in app? Push notifications?
* *Marketing restrictions* -  what is the scope of this question? Push notifications? OOH ads? Specific categories? Latvia has additional restrictions on energy drinks. Estonia has restrictions on alcohol promotions.

“*Passenger Service Fee*” means a service fee charged to you by Bolt for each Journey. When a Passenger Service Fee is applicable, the estimated Passenger Service Fee will be shown as a component of the Fare in the App. More information on how Passenger Service Fees are calculated is available [+here+|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-gb/articles/360019450820].

*Passenger Service Fee*

Where applicable this fee will be charged as part of the fare, calculated at a percentage on top of the fare for a journey or as a fixed fee.

The estimated fare shown in the app will take into account any estimated Passenger Service Fee that applies and any applicable percentage rate will be displayed in the app. Passenger Service Fees will not be calculated on any Congestion Charges, Toll Road fees or airport fees.

For example, if an 8% Passenger Service Fee applied to a £10.80 fare, the Passenger Service Fee would comprise £0.80 of the total fare. Other additional fees may apply to your journey as is set out in this FAQ.

* to be able to issue accurate manual compensations

for London: 
Driver fare = (Total fare - Passenger Service Fee - Toll fee) x 0,8 + Toll fee
For RoUK:
Driver fare = (Total fare - Passenger Service Fee - Toll fee) x 0,85 + Toll fee

As Bolt has a contractual relationship with the Customer and the User, personal data may be required for solving any dispute that may arise from the agreement. Therefore the data will be stored by Bolt as a data controller until the term provided by the law (limitation period for possible claims).

We assure that when the Customer’s account has been deactivated, the the data which we hold will and can only be used to meet legal obligations, accounting and dispute resolution purposes. Confidentiality and security of the data is guaranteed throughout the storage period.

I hope this helps!!

Liis

_We want to draw your attention to this matter that from January 1, 2023 enters into force the Act no. 250/2022 which amends Act no. 442/2012 Coll. on international assistance and cooperation in tax administration, according to which digital platforms must automatically provide information about their clients to tax authorities. [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] - I am coming at this slight behind as only recently joining. However, my understanding is yes, we have purchased insurance for all riders liability. But it is either done via a General Liability (GL) or a Motor Liability (MTPL). policy. 

The GL policy is a non-compulsory insurance meaning if a user breaks the rules or law then the insurer can refuse to pay the damages. The MTPL policy is a compulsory cover. Therefore, regardless of the user breaking the conditions or rules they have to pay any third party damages. You are right in FR it is MTPL and also believe we have MTPL also in Denmark, Germany and Malta.  

However, all other countries are GL and the limits of cover varies.

Hope this helps

Hi all,

Please see below the external counsel’s feedback on parking fines in Portugal:



_The Decree-Law No. 102-B/2020, in force since the beginning of 2021, aimed to legislate the use of electric scooters to ensure order and safety. Until then, this means of transport was not regulated. The Portuguese legislation is now in line with the measures adopted internationally for these vehicles._

_According to Article 112 (3, b) of the Highway Code, electric scooters are subject to the same rules as bicycles. In practice, this means that: you must obey all traffic rules; you must not exceed 25 km/h; you must not use a cell phone or earphones while driving; you must not lift the front or rear wheel when starting off or while driving; you must not drive with your hands off the handlebars; and you must not drive under the influence of alcohol._

_As for non-compliance with the rules, paragraph 6 of art. 112 of the Highway Code: "Whoever circulates on a scooter or circulation device with an electric, self-balancing and self-propelled motor or similar means of circulation with a motor, equipped with a maximum continuous power exceeding 0.25 kW, or reaches a maximum speed of more than 25 km/h, in disregard of the technical characteristics and circulation regime provided for in the previous paragraph, shall be punished by a fine of between 60 and 300 euros"._

_Regarding to parking, it should be noted that in cities where electric scooters circulate, in addition to applying the rules for cyclists, there are hotspots, the name given to places where they are parked when nobody is using them, which drivers should use._

_Under the terms of the article 169, paragraph 6 of the Highway Code, light fines for improper parking of equipment are charged by the Municipality of Lisbon, and it is the responsibility of the Municipal Police and the Lisbon Municipal Mobility and Parking Company (EMEL), within the scope of their competences, to raise the infraction notices._

_Fines will be passed on to users if they are caught in the act and to companies if the user is not on site. The companies will then be able to eventually force users to pay this amount, via the app._

_As provided in article 170 paragraph 1 (a) of the Highway Code the record of the fine must mention the facts constituting the offence, the day, time, place and circumstances in which it was committed, the name and capacity of the authority or authority agent who witnessed it, the identification of the perpetrators of the offence and, when possible, of at least one witness who can testify to the facts the value recorded and the value calculated after deduction of the maximum admissible error provided for in the regulations on metrological control of measuring methods and instruments, where they exist._

_Regarding the identification of the offender, article 171, paragraph 5 of the Highway Code states that when the police officer is unable to identify the offender and verifies that the holder of the identification document is a legal person, that legal person should be notified to identify the driver within 15 working days. Paragraph 6 of the same article states that when notified to do so, the legal person must, within 15 working days, identify the driver of the vehicle at the time of the infraction, indicating all the elements set out in paragraph 1, the legal person must, within 15 working days, identify the driver of the vehicle at the time of the offence, indicating all the elements provided for in paragraph 1, and in case of failure the proceedings will be brought against the legal person._

_Regarding the communication of the fine and the possibilities of defense, Article 175 of the Highway Code stipulates that:_

_"1- After the drawing up of the auto, the defendant shall be notified:_

_a) The facts constituting the infraction;_

_b) The legislation infringed and that which sanctions the facts_

_c) The applicable sanctions;_

_d) The time limit and place for the presentation of the defense, as well as the time limit and place for the presentation of the application for special mitigation or suspension of the accessory sanction_

_e) The possibility of voluntary payment of the fine by the minimum under the terms and with the effects established in Article 172, the possibility of lodging a deposit under the terms and effects referred to in Article 173, the time limit and method for making such deposit, as well as the consequences of failure to pay_

_f) The possibility of requesting the payment of the fine in instalments, at the place and time indicated for presenting the defense_

_g) The time limit for identifying the offender, under the terms and for the purposes provided for in Article 171, paragraphs 3 and 5._

_2 - The defendant may, within 15 working days, counting from the notification_

_a) Make voluntary payment of the fine, under the terms and with the effects set out in Article 172;_

_b) Present a defense and, if so desired, call witnesses, up to a limit of three, and other means of evidence;_

_c) To request special mitigation or suspension of the accessory sanction and, if they so wish, to call witnesses, up to a limit of three, and other means of proof_

_d) Request payment of the fine in instalments, provided that the minimum value of the applicable fine is equal to or greater than 2 UC._

_3 - The defense and the requests provided for in the previous point must be submitted in writing, in Portuguese, and contain the following elements:_

_a) The number of the administrative offence record;_

_b) Identification of the defendant by name;_

_c) Statement of the facts, justification and request;_

_d) Signature of the defendant or, if applicable, of the attorney or legal representative._

_4 - In the defense, the accused shall expressly state the facts on which the evidence is to be based, on pain of having the evidence submitted dismissed._

_5 - The request provided for in paragraph 2(d), as well as the requests to consult the file or to identify the offender under the terms of article 171(3) must be submitted on a form approved by order of the President of ANSR.”(_President of the National Road Safety Authority).

 

_Thus, to answer the questions raised:_

 

*_1- Can these fines be challenged to obtain nullity or at least a reduction in the amount to be paid based on the impossibility of making the payment on time, for instance? If so, please we would like to start challenging the fines as soon as possible._*

_The fines can only be contested if it is established that the notification does not contain all the above-mentioned elements, and within 15 days of notification._

_In any case, if the fines are applied to a legal person, the same must be notified to identify the driver within 15 working days, and if the driver is identified the process will continue against him._

_Regarding the impossibility of making the payments on time, the article 175 paragraph 2 (d), admits the possibility to request payment of the fine in instalments, provided that the minimum value of the applicable fine is equal to or greater than 2 UC, i.e., €204,00. Since the fine applicable in this case is 60 to 300 euros, this request is not possible._

 

*_2- Are the cities legitimised to impose parking fines on scooters and have the right to charge us the same as a larger vehicle without notifying us in any way?_*

_Yes, as stated above according to paragraph 6 of article 169 of the Highway Code light fines for improper parking of equipment are charged by the Municipality of Lisbon, and it is the responsibility of the Municipal Police and the Lisbon Municipal Mobility and Parking Company (EMEL), within the scope of their competences, to raise the infraction notices._

 

*_3- Is Bolt as the owner of the assets and service provider of the scooter ultimately obligated to pay the fines if we are unable to forward the fine to the user?_* 

_Yes, notified of a fine, if within 15 working days, Bolt fails to identify the driver of the vehicle at the time of the infraction, indicating all the elements set out in paragraph 1 of article 171, the proceedings will be brought against Bolt._

 

*_4- Can you suggest any high-level mitigation plan to address this growing concern?_*

_Considering everything we have already explained, our suggestion is that whenever you receive a fine notification, you should send us the notification together with the details of the driver responsible for the vehicle at the date and time of the infraction, so that we can prepare the corresponding defense._



In short, according to the Highway Code, Municipalities have the legitimacy to fine scooter companies. Considering the above conclusions, we wanted to ask the external counsel if we can sue/go after the Municipalities for the limited time that the Municipalities allow to pay fines, which according to what you initially told us is two hours a day. However, [~accountid:62e0e5a93257defaf50d1e34]  confirmed that the fines can be paid from 7:30 am to 10 pm. Can we have a call next week to clarify this point and agree on next steps? 

Many thanks!

Hiya!

Blocking or blacklisting _driver devices_ does not restrict _rider devices_ from being used. This means that if we blacklist a driver device, the driver can still use this device for rider accounts. 

Furthermore, device UID (the tokens you have noted down on the sheet) are not reliable for permanent or extensive action. For example, if the driver would be to reset the same device, a new UID can be created again and our restrictions would not react as it is not the same UID anymore. So it is not an effective way to mitigate drivers from using the service/signing up. 

We would rather recommend focusing on suspending the driver accounts that are fraudulent/misusing the service and putting more emphasis on the onboarding process in general.

Part of [https://github.com/bolteu/react-commons/pull/578|https://github.com/bolteu/react-commons/pull/578|smart-link] simplified the babel config in test apps to bare minimum and metro configuration seems to cover all the Monorepo needs now.

One problem that can still come up is: due to assumptions in expo metro config {{node-linker=hoisted}} was used and in addition to creating a flat node_modules without symlinking the setting might hoist common project deps to the root node_modules. Looks like there’s no way to have yarn workspaces {{no-hoist}} behaviour for this on pnpm with the setting.

The hoisting to root node_modules can cause issues with cocoapods, gradle where RN ecosystem makes a lot of assumptions, but they can be patched/fixed as suggested here [https://www.callstack.com/blog/setting-up-react-native-monorepo-with-yarn-workspaces|https://www.callstack.com/blog/setting-up-react-native-monorepo-with-yarn-workspaces|smart-link] and referenced [https://docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos/#script--does-not-exist|https://docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos/#script--does-not-exist|smart-link]

[~accountid:630725a2d53432606c498bc2] proposed the idea of having the test app outside of pnpm workspaces scope and symlink the local dependecies to avoid the hoisting to root, which actually looks promising and would better mimic the behaviour of consumers. The initial downsides we could think of were the additional overhead of running TS/eslint linting as {{pnpm -r lint:js}}, extending tsconfig, eslint from root etc wouldn’t work. 

Worth also looking into internal logic of pnpm and perhaps it’s easy to disable the hoisting to root.

In general it is not per se forbidden to monitor individual employee performance. 

However, there are several steps that we need to take in such case: 

a) identifying a lawful basis under GDPR. The most appropriate would be legitimate interest which requires a separate assessment and weighing individual employee and employer interests. 

b) Employers must make workers aware of the nature, extent and reasons for the monitoring. Therefore we need notify our employees transparently of how such audit logs being used to measure performance. 

c) Employers must be clear about their purpose for monitoring. Therefore it needs to be clear what is the purpose of using this data. For example is the purpose only to fix the processes or may this also bring any consequences to the employee as well.

Hey!

This is an interesting question. ECA states the following:

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
h3. *§ 74.*  Specifications for compensation for damage

 (1) If an employee has intentionally breached the employment contract, they are liable for all damage caused to the employer as a result of the breach.

 (2) If an employee has breached the employment contract due to negligence, they are liable for the damage caused to the employer to the extent which is determined taking into account the employee's duties, level of guilt, instructions given to the employee, working conditions, risk arising from the nature of the work, the length of employment with the employer, behaviour so far, the employee's wages, and also reasonably expected possibilities of the employer for reduction or insurance of damage. Compensation is reduced by the damage caused as a result of a typical risk of damage relating to the activities of the employer.
{panel}



So, we have to look at the situation from the PoV if we were the employer. 

* Did we suffer damages? Yes
* Were the pickers instructed? Yes
* Was the equipment is good working order? Yes?
* Did the picker have to check if the door was closed after using it? Yes?

So I think we could argue that the picker was negligent and we can claim direct damages. To what extent? If we can find documents stating that they were instructed how the fridge must be used and what is the procedure for checking the state of the fridge, I’d say to the fullest extent (this means damages for the goods + reasonable expenses for ordering new ones).  

As this is B2B relationship, I’d reason that the picker was instructed and knew how the fridge should be operated and this gives us grounds for claiming the damages. And for the damages - direct + reasonable costs [utilization of spoiled goods, ordering new goods etc], (and should there be negotiations, the reasonable costs for ordering new goods can be dropped).

* by trying to resolve it, the probability of breaking something is high; it can lead to corner cases like this: (mixing old and new builder) 

[https://taxify.slack.com/archives/GDTRN8MUZ/p1667476436963589|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/GDTRN8MUZ/p1667476436963589|smart-link]

* the impact is not that big and can be isolated ( it only happens when you have inconsistency in your deployments, which shouldn’t be the case ( different hosts have different package versions) or deploy for the first time a package to the k8s.

The first case ( different hosts with different package versions):

# deploy v1 to host1, host2, host3

# deploy v2 to host1, host2

# deploy v3 to host1, host2, host3

# rollback to v2 -> hos1 and host2 will be reverted to v2 and host3 to v1.

The second case (deploy for the first time a package to the k8s)

# deploy v1 to host1, host2

# deploy v2 to host1, host2, k8s_host

# rollback to v1 -> host1 and host2 will be reverted to v1 and k8s_host will fail to revert to v1 because there are no deploy_params on that version. This case is isolated because this is not something usual. Someone from the PINT team will do this until k8s deployments are fully integrated.

* I have rewritten the Redshift queries: “search_categories”, “rider_features” and “cat_groups”.
*  I have not rewritten “user_created”, as it currently is not used by the model. Note that omitting “user_created” requires small changes in the preprocessing code, where the “user_created” data is loaded but not used.

The only major changes were to the “search_categories” table. Here is an overview:


*Performance changes:*

 1) Removed the second search_category_overview_categories join and replaced strange groupby (GROUP by 1,2,...,16) and row_number() rank with dense rank.  

2) Changed pricing.price_prediction_result_rate join from LEFT JOIN to INNER join 

3) Removed core.company_order_tries completely  

*Redshift query* (literal presto translation) performance (2 days of data, some cities) : *20 minutes*  

*Spark query performance* (2 days of data, some cities) : *4 minutes*   



*Data differences between Redshift query and spark query:*
1) There was a *bug* in the Redshift query. *order_tries were not joined based on city_id* and therefore non-finished orders were added to the result, as the order_id may have matched a finished order from a different city. For example, consider a cancelled order with id=12345 in Tallinn (city_id=1), which was never finished. The order with id=12345 in London was finished. Hence, the order=12345 in Tallinn is considered a "finished" order. This affected about (17000 / 1212194) = 1.4% of orders.

 2) *Removed company_order_tries completely*. Finished orders is determined based on company_order state instead. This lead to a decrease of (115 / 1212194) = 0.009% orders. These are orders that are placed shortly before midnight or scheduled rides, that have their order_try accepted only on the next day. For example, if the query has end_date 2022-10-20 and an order is placed at 2022-10-20 23:59:59 and the order_try is accepted at 2022-10-21 00:00:05, then the order will be excluded with the company_order_try join and included with the exclusion of the company_order_try join.    

Note that this also removed columns "reject_reason" and "order_try_id". These do not appear in preprocessing, but we need to check that this does not break anything.   

3) *Changed LEFT JOIN to INNER JOIN for pricing.price_prediction_result_rate*. This leads to the removal of orders that do not have prices, which we exclude from predictions in Best-Offer anyways. This removed (90 / 1212169) = 0.007% of the orders. 

4) Sometimes different search_categories_overview_tokens have the same search_category_overview.created time (I do not know why). Hence, as we choose the last search_categories_overview_token of the order based on created time, we cannot differentiate this case. In the Redshift query, the ranking function row_number would randomly choose one of the two tokens. In the spark query, we add search_categories_overview_token as a tie-breaking rank condition. Essentially, both queries are choosing the correct token randomly and therefore they may choose different tokens.

{noformat}sql_test2 = """
WITH order_search_tmp as (
    select
        s.user_id,
        s.session_id,
        s.search_categories_overview_token,
        s.price_prediction_token,
        s.surge_token,
        s.created,
        sc.no_of_drivers,
        s.lat,
        s.lng,
        sc.search_category_id as cat_id,
        sc.pos,
        sc.duration_till_pickup as eta,
        s.search_token,
        best_offer_category_id,
        _order.id as order_id,
        _order.state as state,
        cast(sf.filter_search_category_id as SMALLINT) as order_cat,
        min(sc.search_category_id) over (partition by sc.search_categories_overview_token) = max(sc.search_category_id) over (partition by sc.search_categories_overview_token) as single_cat,
        s.city_id
    from core.search_categories_overview_category as sc
        inner join core.search_categories_overview as s on (
                sc.search_categories_overview_token = s.search_categories_overview_token
                and s.city_id in ({city_ids})
                and s.created_hour >= DATE('{start_date}') and s.created_hour < DATE('{end_date}')
        )
        inner join ng_public_spark.company_order as _order on (
            s.session_id = _order.session_id
            and s.city_id = _order.city_id
            and s.created < _order.created
            and _order.state = 'finished'
            and _order.created_date >= DATE('{start_date}') and _order.created_date < DATE('{end_date}')
            and _order.city_id in ({city_ids})
            
        )
        inner join ng_public_spark.company_order_search_filter as sf on (
            _order.id = sf.id
            and _order.city_id = sf.city_id
        )
    where true
        and sc.created_hour >= DATE('{start_date}') AND sc.created_hour < DATE('{end_date}')
)
, multi_cat_searches as (
    select
        *,
        --search_categories_overview_token breaks ties when two tokens have same created time
        dense_rank() over (partition by order_id, city_id order by created desc, search_categories_overview_token desc) as cat_token_rank
    from order_search_tmp
    where true 
        and not single_cat
)
select 
    ms.user_id,
    ms.session_id,
    ms.search_categories_overview_token,
    ms.price_prediction_token,
    ms.surge_token,
    ms.created,
    ms.no_of_drivers,
    ms.lat,
    ms.lng,
    ms.cat_id,
    ms.pos,
    ms.eta,
    ms.city_id,
    ms.search_token,
    ms.best_offer_category_id,
    prr.distance,
    prr.duration,
    prr.surge_multiplier as surge,
    prr.predicted_price,
    prr.predicted_discounted_price,
    ms.order_id,
    ms.state,
    ms.order_cat
from multi_cat_searches ms

        and ms.cat_id = prr.search_category_id
        and prr.created_hour between DATE('{start_date}') and DATE('{end_date}')
)
where true
    and cat_token_rank = 1

{noformat}(select source_type, s3_key, document_type, country, doc_side from (
