Q: Wouldn't 👆 select only docs with country = 'ES? (if there are at least 10 of them)?

A: Yes, but that is on the user triggering the query to choose wisely.
If I want 500 incorrect docs and I select 100 per doc, then it's very likely I'll end up with 5 ES docs only (assuming we have 5 different ES docs).
If I go with 50 instead the situation might change. Of course if we have 10 different ES docs we have the same problem.
But I think it might be better to have 500 ES docs not being IDs rather than a bunch of docs from countries Spaniards never see.

The solution would be to ask users ([~accountid:5dd7a2cab5933d0eefaf7d1e] being the first) to reduce the {{max_number_of_samples_per_incorrect_label}} from 50 (what we usually do) to say 30.

h2. *Query* 👇

{code:sql}with vmsmf as (
select content_type_id, path, context
from ng_public.verification_media_storage_media_file
where content_type = 'document'
  and created_date between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-08-01'
)
,ivfr as (
select user_id, uuid, document_type
from ng_public.identity_verification_flow_run
where status = 'verified'
	and created_date between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-08-01'
)
,ivd as (
select flow_run_uuid, id, upper(country) as country, type 
from ng_public.identity_verification_document
where created_date between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-08-01'
)
,correct_docs as (
select * from (
    select 'veritas' as source_type,
        ivd.type as document_type,
        ivd.country,
        row_number() over (partition by ivfr.user_id) as r,
        concat('live/', vmsmf.path) as s3_key,
        vmsmf.context as doc_side
    from ivfr
        join ivd on ivfr.uuid = ivd.flow_run_uuid
            and ivfr.document_type = 'identity_card'
            and ivd.country = 'ES'
        join vmsmf on vmsmf.content_type_id = ivd.id
            and vmsmf.context = 'front')
where r = 1
)
,incorrect_docs as (
select * from (
    select 'veritas' as source_type,
        ivd.type as document_type,
        ivd.country,
        row_number() over (partition by ivd.country, ivfr.document_type) as r,
        concat('live/', vmsmf.path) as s3_key,
        vmsmf.context as doc_side
    from ivfr
    join ivd on ivfr.uuid = ivd.flow_run_uuid
    join vmsmf on vmsmf.content_type_id = ivd.id
    where ivfr.document_type != 'identity_card' or ivd.country != 'ES'
    )     
where r <= 2
)   	
(select source_type, s3_key, document_type, country, doc_side from correct_docs limit 10)
union all
(select source_type, s3_key, document_type, country, doc_side from (
	select * from incorrect_docs where country = 'ES'
    union all
    select * from incorrect_docs where country != 'ES'
)
limit 10){code}

Hey team, we need to amend the EU Driver T&Cs in connection with *the implementation of DAC7 directive*.Yesterday tax team had a meeting with EE tax authority, and it is moretheless clear now what we need to amend in our T&Cs.

# *What is DAC7?* Directive that extends EU tax transparency rules to online marketplaces and requires reporting seller data to tax authorities.
# *Who are the sellers in the context of DAC7?* In the context of ride hailing, the sellers are drivers and fleets (depending on fleet’s type).
# *What is the data to be reported to the tax authority?*

* Name
* Primary address
* Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), in the absence of TIN place of birth
* VAT ID
* date of birth in case of the private person, business registration number and the existence of any permanent establishment through which relevant activities are carried out

*4. What is the data we already collect from the drivers and fleets and what is new?* Please find the whole overview per each market here [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dsLTf0OBPoshTEqF3G4A-ew5UFRlPBBRnxQmY6UmYZc/edit#gid=1438907228|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dsLTf0OBPoshTEqF3G4A-ew5UFRlPBBRnxQmY6UmYZc/edit#gid=1438907228|smart-link]

*5. What do we need to amend in our T&Cs?* Under DAC7 as of 1 January 2023 we are allowed to either terminate the drivers or freeze drivers’ payouts if no information or incorrect information is provided to us within 60 days after our notification to the drivers. The termination option is mostly reflected in our T&Cs as a legal basis to terminate the driver under the laws but payouts freeze option is not provided in our T&Cs. Therefore, we need to add it to the T&Cs of all markets across the EU.

*6. How business decided to implement the above?*

* new drivers seeking access to our platform from 1 Jan 2023
** if information is incorrect or not provided within 60-day period we are blocking them (terminating the agreements with them)
** no freeze of payouts is applied (TBC with @maret and @margarita.olshanskaya)
* existing drivers
** we freeze payouts to the drivers who have not provided us with correct information within 60-day period
** there is no plan to terminate / block existing drivers from the platform due to not providing or providing incorrect information to us (TBC with [@maret|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U5SK1DXC4] and [@margarita.olshanskaya|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U03QZDSV6AJ])

*7. Action points for now*

* Please take a look at the Driver T&Cs of your markets and check:
** whether there is a general provision on our right to request information from drivers (in global T&Cs there is a section 2.1 that reflects that right),
** please review the wording to ensure we have reflected the right of passing information to tax authority. Although there is no obligation to reflect this, since we are amending T&Cs anyway, I would include this wording to the T&Cs: Bolt is entitled to share with the relevant tax authorities any information required under Council Directive (EU) 2021/514 of 22 March 2021 amending Directive 2011/16/EU on administrative cooperation in the field of taxation, including but not limited to any consideration paid or credited to the Driver in connection with the activities carried out through the Bolt Platform.
** whether there are any obstacles for freezing the payouts under the local laws (I assume there are no obstacles to this, since our right stems directly from DAC7 and thus, should be implemented in the local laws)
*  Please reach out to me if you are currently in the process of amending local T&Cs and let’s align on how to add DAC7 amendments to your planned amendments.

*8. Action points for myself.* I will:

* once driver termination and payouts freeze process is clear, I will come up with the wording to reflect payouts freeze in our T&Cs and submit it for your review,
* once done and aligned, I would kindly ask you to add the wording to your local T&Cs, translate the new amendments, and upload updated T&Cs to the legal landing page (please reach out to me if you need help with this one),
* talk to project managers with regard to communications of the T&C changes - rides leads would like to do it in a way that would not hurt much our supply across the Europe.
Tickets. I will make a ticket with multiple subtickets where we would be able to align. 
Feel free to reach out to me directly or post in a thread if there are any questions, comments or suggestions.

*9. Deadline.* The amendments should enter into force on 1 January 2023. Considering the 15-day notice period for Drivers in most markets, we will need to upload updated T&Cs to our legal landing page the latest on 16 December 2022.

Thanks a lot everyone for your continuous support!

Julia

When it comes to the use of 3rd party data, we have to always 
1) verify whether the 3rd party allows the data to be used by us; and if yes

2) under what circumstances (open source maps usually still require an acknowledgement in the app - if you open Uber app - Account - Legal - Data providers - you will see how Uber acknowledges its map data providers).

I understand you want to use the map data of the different providers linked above. The least riskiest and preferred approach would be to contact the provider, ask for their permission to use the data (for free) and record the agreement in writing. This way we eliminate any risk of misunderstanding the data use license/ copyright terms. I can help you with recording the agreement/ consent in writing - the document would have to (1) identify the data; (2) what it’s used for by Bolt; (3) price - for free; (4) period of use - forever.

I know it might be difficult to reach the providers and it might look like a burdensome exercise to record the consent in writing but only this way we will eliminate any risks related to the potential breach of 3rd party intellectual property (something we cannot afford with the prospect of potential IPO in the coming years).

If the above approach is not acceptable, we can try to review the license terms linked above. As the licenses are in local languages, I would have to engage local law firms and ask for their help. The main difference in price comes from the duration of the journey and is caused by factors out of the driver’s hands such as heavy traffic. This means that the trip was charged based on the actual time and distance, not the estimated one. While the route is not exactly the same, the driver has followed the most optimal way to the destination for that time of the day based on the road conditions. 

Our suggestion would be to explain to the customer that an estimate is just that - an estimated price not taking into account the current forces at play on the actual road. You may follow your local guidelines regarding price disputes and compensate the rider accordingly.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] , 

Thank you so much for your inputs. 

From a Spanish law perspective, we should distinguish between i) independent drivers (self-employed drivers who hold a VTC license) and ii) fleet drivers (drivers who work for a fleet). 

i) According to article 1.3 g) of Royal Legislative Decree 2/2015, of 23 March, on the Statute of Workers (hereinafter, “SW”), drivers rendering transport services with their own vehicles under a mandatory administrative licence (that is, independent drivers) are excluded from the application of labour law. Therefore, in principle, any person rendering services in the aforementioned circumstances will not hold an employment relationship, even if they just render services to one client or mainly to one client. 

In this regard, we can consider that independent drivers rendering services as drivers on their own under a VTC licence would be in principle excluded from the application of labour law. Although we cannot completely discard this risk if there is a change in case-law or in the SW in the future, at the moment I do not consider that applying the driver behaviour filter to independent drivers is a substantial risk in terms of reclassification.  

ii) Regarding fleet drivers, article 43 SW must be taken into account, according to which it will be considered that there is an illegal assignment of employees when any or all of the following circumstances arise:  

# The subject-matter of the service contracts between the undertakings is limited to the mere secondment of the assignor’s employees to the assignee. 
# The assignor does not have its own stable activity or organisation, neither have the means necessary to carry out its activity. 
# The assignor does not exercise the functions inherent to its status as an employer. 

 

Let’s assess if the above circumstances concur when applying the driver filter behaviour:

# In my view, this circumstance does not concur as the fleet drivers may provide transportation services through other platforms of the fleet partners’ choice, hence the subject matter of the agreement between Bolt and Fleet Partners is not limited to mere secondment of the assignor’s employees to the assignee. 
# In my view, this requisite does not concur as the fleet partners have their own stable activity and organisation, being the holders of the VTC licenses and the cars’ owners. 
# Here's the key question:  

* is Bolt exercising an inherent role of an employer by applying driver filter behaviour?  
* Can it be considered that while we are not monitoring the performance of the fleet drivers by giving them direct instructions, we are selecting them based on their performance to provide certain services as an employer could do? 
* Could this selection be considered as an organizational faculty that corresponds to the employers? 

I scheduled a call with Fernando to better understand how this filter will work and also if it will affect driver earnings. Fleet drivers are on a fixed salary as far as I know, but I'm not sure if they get bonuses based on certain KPIs (like online hours, billing, etc.) and this filter might affect their access to those bonuses for instance. 

I will keep you posted and happy to include you in the call if you wish. 

Thank you!

Everything seems to be matching, but I believe the fleet’s confusion is coming from not understanding the schedule/timeline/payouts. So, please educate the fleet.

*Payout*: Payout period is Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59. And the payout for this period is made on the following Tuesday/Wednesday.

*App*: App shows the amount for the selected period. Doesn’t necessarily reflect the payout period. They will need to select the specific week to match their earnings and weekly breakdown. For example, these screenshots show the full month in the app.

*Payout*: Payouts are made based on the previous week’s rides. So, For example, 25.10 payout includes the rides between 18-23.10 week.. Meaning rides between 23th and the payout is not included in the payout, will be included in the next payout. Rule of thumb: payouts happen 2 days after the end of active week. So they are actually payouts of the previous week. But the app will include the rides between the end of the week and until the next payout. But since payout for this week hasn’t been made yet, it will look like they earned more but not got paid. But they will get paid the next Tue/Wed.

So when they match their earnings, they should compare the amount they received and the numbers for the period UNTIL the Sunday right before the payout. Anything after Sunday will be included on next week’s payout.

I’d like to bring up a a concern regarding the approach and the goals outlined here.

Redis locks are indeed convenient to use and lightweight, however they do not really satisfy the safety property if we require mutual exclusion: as locks have expiration time, there can still be more than one actor with an access to the resource at a given time (in case processing takes longer than a timeout, long garbage collector pause, etc). Typical way to address that issue is implementing fencing tokens in the data storage to prevent actors with expired leases from making progress, which is far from being particularly straightforward. More on this: [https://martin.kleppmann.com/2016/02/08/how-to-do-distributed-locking.html|https://martin.kleppmann.com/2016/02/08/how-to-do-distributed-locking.html|smart-link]

My suggestion is to carefully consider each particular use case to figure out whether we’re doing locking for efficiency or safety. In case of the latter, perhaps we should consider a different approach.

Just to clarify the legal background (consumer protection regulation): customer generally has right request a refund using the same means of payment as the consumer used to pay for the service, unless the consumer expressly agrees otherwise. Bolt has decided to take an acknowledged risk, and make the refunds to Bolt Balance, unless the customer complains, in which case a full refund is made to the original payment method (according to the current statistic, only about 2% of customers challenge the refund to Bolt Balance. So our by default refund process is partial refund to Bolt Balance (in all countries except the UK) but if the customer complains, a full refund should be made to their original payment method, please see the new refund process for a detailed description: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/l/cp/Fuz8mq7n|https://taxify.atlassian.net/l/cp/Fuz8mq7n|smart-link]  As far as I understand the updated refund process, currently it is not possible to make partial refunds to the original payment method (the feature will be developed in the future), so only full refund is possible. Please let me know if you have any questions. If you have specific questions regarding the updated process - please refer these to Bolt Balance PM Katie Chang.

*Replacing per-vehicle features in rental_fleet with per-vehicle disabled features in rentl_car_vehicle*

All vehicles in live that have any per-vehicle features +enabled+ also have these features enabled for their models. So the migration from rental_fleet.car_vehicle_*feature*_link to rental_car_vehicle.vehicle_*disabled_feature*_link looks pretty straightforward.

The query to check this attached below:

{noformat}select
    model.display_name, f.name_default,
    if(exists(select 0 from car_vehicle_model_feature_link mod_link where mod_link.feature_id = veh_link.feature_id and car.model_id = mod_link.model_id), 'yes', 'no') as redundant
from car_vehicle_feature_link veh_link
    join car_vehicle_feature f on f.id = veh_link.feature_id
    join car_vehicle car on car.id = veh_link.vehicle_id
    join car_vehicle_model model on model.id = car.model_id
where veh_link.is_active = 1;{noformat}
